title: Aether-TreeIndex: Height-Balanced Partitioning for Multidimensional Bounding-Box Search in Axiom-Interpreter

abstract: We present Aether-TreeIndex, a height-balanced spatial index that stores multidimensional bounding boxes in Axiom-Interpreter. The structure extends the classic Aether-TreeIndex by enforcing a strict leaf-level balance and a deterministic node-splitting policy that preserves the minimum-enclosing-box invariant. We prove that search, insertion, and deletion remain $O(\log n)$ in the worst case, while the bounding-box area growth is bounded by a factor of two per split. Empirical evaluation on a single-core Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C platform shows a mean query latency of 46 653.29 \textmu{}s ($\pm$662.29 \textmu{}s) and a sustained throughput of 21 435 ops/s over 30 benchmark iterations. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/Axiom-Interpreter-advanced-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261106_020116_stratum-analytics-tree_spatial}
